newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF CHELSEA V MAN UTD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF CHELSEA V MAN UTD.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Chelsea and Manchester United who meet in the English premier league on Saturday (1500 GMT).

Playing style: England manager Glenn Hoddle introduced wingbacks to Chelsea during his spell as player-manager and Ruud Gullit has carried on where Hoddle left off. Dan Petrescu and Scott Minto play the wide roles with Frenchman Frank Leboeuf anchoring the defence. Gullit is a staunch advocate of what he likes to call "sexy football". Chelsea play short passes to feet, aiming to release Gianfranco Zola or Gianluca Vialli through the channels. Mark Hughes adds a touch of Welsh grit just behind either of the two Italians.

Strengths: Individual players capable of turning a match. Zola has been a revelation since his arrival from Parma in November. Vialli shone early in the season and although he has often been relegated to the bench since then he is still potentially devastating. United old boy Hughes is as combative as ever and Lebouef and Di Matteo ensure class is not limited to Chelsea's front line.
Weaknesses: Chelsea's midfielders and defenders -- Leboeuf and di Matteo excepted -- are not of the same calibre as their forwards. Goalkeeper Kevin Hitchcock is inconsistent.

Motivation: Victory would catapult Chelsea back into the title race. Defeat would leave them a massive 15 points behind United, albeit with two games in hand. They still nurse memories of two painful F.A. Cup defeats -- 4-0 in the 1994 final and 2-1 in last year's semifinal.

Playing style: A basic 4-3-3 style but in name only as manager Alex Ferguson changes his playing style to suit the occasion. Traditionally Manchester United play expansively, attacking down the flanks or coming through the middle with equal ease.

Strengths: Proven class in almost every position with players of great flair and vision like Eric Cantona, Ryan Giggs and David Beckham capable of turning a match in a flash. The driving force of Roy Keane adds steel to an already tough framework.

Weaknesses: The volatile temperament of Keane, and to a lesser extent these days, Cantona. Some inexperience among younger players has cost United matches, most notably against Fenerbahce and Juventus in the European Champions' League late last year.

Motivation: Revenge for Chelsea's 2-1 win at Old Trafford in November which ended an unbeaten home league record stretching back to late 1994. Ferguson's side are out of the F.A. Cup and therefore retaining their league title is all the more important. They will want to amass as many league points as possible before turning their attentions back to Europe in a fortnight's time. Defeat could cost them top spot in the table.
